title: Marriage to Dorothy Williams and the breakup
summary: He recounts marrying Dorothy Williams, their daughter, the divorce, and returning to Chicago and the Three Deuces.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Now you mentioned children. And I do know that you've been married twice. And we need some vital statistics here. Now your first wife was....

My first wife was Dorothy Williams of the Williams' Sisters. They were singers and dancers. And they were very good the Williams' Sisters. They recorded and it was swinging, they were swinging. And her name was Dorothy Williams and we had a baby called Dorothy our daughter. And that was while I was in the show Buddy Rose's 'Crazy Quilt'. Dorothy and I were married, we had a baby and Hannah, her sister, went into Buddy Rose's 'Crazy Quilt' with Fanny Brice, Bill Baker, Ted Healy, James Barton, Georgie Jessel. And I was in the pit. Playing in the pit.

And we went along like that for about a year I guess and then the show went on the road. And Hannah, no before the show went on the road, Hannah Williams married Roger Wolfe Kahn the international banker's son. And she married Roger Wolfe Kahn and Dorothy, my wife, took her place in the show. For a while. But then the show went on the road and Dorothy didn't go. They got somebody else. She stayed in New York with the baby.

To take care of the baby and I went on the road with the show. And when I came back why she had gotten together with her sister and they were both, I mean Hannah was going to get a divorce from Roger Wolf Kahn and my wife decided to divorce me and marry somebody with a lot of money. And that broke me up. That's the thing that, that's the thing that broke me up.

So I just, as a matter of fact, I went down to New Orleans with Glen Miller and Smith Bullew and Ray McKinley was on drums then. And worked down there for six months. But when I came back, seeing the whole situation. Dorothy had gotten married again, my wife and had gotten the baby, she had the baby and everything so I just sort of lost heart, you know. And not knowing how to cope with the situation, I just couldn't even play.

So I decided to go back to Chicago which I did and join my brother with a little outfit called the 'Embassy Four'Quartet' and we played that in the Dalmer House for a little while. And then I didn't care for that, it was too commercial, the music was. And I decided to get my own band. That's when I went into the 'Three Deuces' there. Billie Holiday, Anita O'Day was my girl singer in my band. But Billie Holiday
was in the floor show. And as I mentioned before, Art Tatum was the intermission piano player. And I finally came out of it.
